name: Entity Graph
blurb: Every company, model, paper, person, dataset, benchmark, and regulation as a node.

nodes.scheme: DOI or arXiv id, linked to the original publisher
arXiv id from the model's own tags
registry id from the official MCP registry

reading.body:
The graph indexes 23,341 nodes across 16 categories, and its shape reveals where AI complexity actually concentrates: open models alone account for 15,255 of those nodes, more than 65 percent of the total, dwarfing every other category combined.

That asymmetry matters for anyone trying to understand AI scaling. The 15,255 open models tracked by Hugging Face repository ID sit alongside only 418 API models and 37 hardware entries. The hardware count is the sharpest signal: a vast proliferation of models rests on a substrate that this graph represents with fewer entries than the number of tracked lawsuits. Whether those 37 hardware entries cover the full range of chips, accelerators, and interconnects in active use, or only a curated subset, the data does not say. What it does say is that the model layer is orders of magnitude more crowded than the infrastructure layer beneath it.

The regulatory surface is also large and fragmented. State AI bills number 3,013, which is more than any other single category and nearly ten times the count of open companies tracked. The graph does not record which bills passed, which are active, or how they distribute across jurisdictions, so no compliance burden can be inferred from the count alone. The 109 lawsuits and 67 compliance documents add further legal surface area, but again the data covers existence, not outcome or severity. Readers wanting to understand regulatory risk will find the shape of the problem here, not its resolution.
